title: Blood glucose report
body: Ravi, a 45-year-old office worker, visited a clinic complaining of frequent urination, constant thirst and tiredness. Tests over three months showed that his fasting blood glucose stayed well above the normal range. His urine contained glucose, and it also contained ketone bodies. The doctor explained that in a healthy person, the hormones of the Islets of Langerhans keep blood glucose within narrow limits: one hormone acts mainly on hepatocytes to raise blood glucose, while the other acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes to lower it. Ravi was started on a hormone therapy and advised regular monitoring.
